column1: # Engine wave W5 (18 Oct 2026, rulings R136–R138): the regional safe default for the Levant (`default.safe.levant`,
# Generic.kt; spec §6.2 c: Israel), gated for the first time, as a stress test only: no table was thought held for Israel,
# so it is checked against its neighbours' tables, each with its own entry and never routed here: Jordan's Awqaf
# at Amman (the 2025 captures and the monitor's pinned region table of 2 Oct 2026), the PA's perpetual al-Aqsa
# table (2026, printed on the winter clock all year, hence `clock`, as ps-iftaa.tsv has it) and Lebanon's Dar
# al-Fatwa at Beirut (2026, the same fixed clock, as lb-fatwa.tsv has it). Every row is held out. Nothing is
# What the rows show is the cost of the region's design (its late limits, Generic.kt, levantLateLimits): Fajr
# 9 to 17 min after Lebanon's 20° dawn (this region's Fajr is the 18° in use in Jordan and Palestine) and up to
# 6 min after Jordan's and the PA's own 18° with their minutes; Isha (Jordan's 18.2° + 2 min) up to 10 min after
# Lebanon's and 6 after the PA's; the end of eating (the 20° dawn − 2 min, Lebanon's) 10 to 16 min before the
# 18° Fajr Jordan and the PA print; and sunrise and sunset at the −2.25° horizon Jordan and the PA use (about
# 7 min outside the sun's edge) with the floors and the cushion on top: sunrise up to 14 min before Beirut's
# printed one, Maghrib up to 10 min after, Dhuhr up to 7, Asr up to 5.
# REAL ROWS, added by the safe defaults lane (12 Nov 2026): the archive does hold tables for Israel. The PA Dar al-Iftaa
# prints its al-Aqsa table for thirteen towns in Israel by a figure each (ssalah2012.pdf p. 2: Nazareth and Umm al-Fahm
# + 0; Tiberias, Safed and Beisan - 1; Haifa, Acre, Kafr Qasim and Tayibe + 1; Lydd and Ramla + 1.5; Beersheba and Jaffa
# + 2), held as derived tables for 2026 and 2027 (archive/tables/manual/ps-iftaa/2026-10-02/, ps-iftaa.tsv reads them for
# its units). Who in Israel follows them is not surveyed (the engine survey: "the owner needs local evidence"), but they
# are the Palestinian authority's own times for Arab towns in Israel, so they plausibly reflect local practice and are
# held to the promise here, each at the app's own city point (Lydd and Ramla in their starts and ends files, as
# ps-iftaa.tsv). They found this region's Fajr a minute early on 474 of 9,490 place-days (Acre, Safed, Nazareth and the
# other northern towns, May to July: the table's al-Aqsa dawn moved by a whole minute, against the town's own 18° dawn
# with the cushion, which came up to 133 s before it). The fix (Generic.kt's levant, fajrExtraSeconds = 138, the excess
# + 5 s): Israel's Fajr 138 s later everywhere, read off these rows, so they are fit rows (the stress rows stay held
# out). After it: 0 early, 0 late ends; Fajr up to 10 min after the PA's, Isha
# up to 11, Maghrib 11, sunrise 14 before, the end of eating up to 23 before (the 20° dawn - 2 against the PA's 18°).
